messages.subject: Odd behavior in timer()
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I've been using the timer function for quite a while and wanted to report an odd behavior.

If you apply the function and that your envelope is above your threshold right at the start or end of your signal,
the first start.signal or the last end.signal value, respectively, is missing.
Of course, a simple trick would be to add silence at the begining or the end of the signal but I've come up with a simple fix.
I replaced:

if (wave2[1] == 1) {
        first <- "pause"
        pause <- durations[seq(1, npos - 1, by = 2)]
        signal <- durations[seq(2, npos - 1, by = 2)]
        start.signal <- positions[seq(2, npos - 1, by = 2)]
        end.signal <- positions[seq(3, npos - 1, by = 2)]
    }
    else {
        first <- "signal"
        pause <- durations[seq(2, npos - 1, by = 2)]
        signal <- durations[seq(1, npos - 1, by = 2)]
        start.signal <- positions[seq(1, npos - 1, by = 2)]
        end.signal <- positions[seq(2, npos - 1, by = 2)]
    }

By:

if (wave2[1] == 1) {
        first <- "pause"
        pause <- durations[seq(1, npos - 1, by = 2)]
        signal <- durations[seq(2, npos - 1, by = 2)]
        start.signal <- positions[seq(2, npos - 1, by = 2)]
        end.signal <- positions[seq(3, npos - 1, by = 2)]
        if (start.signal < end.signal) end.signal <- c(end.signal, length(wave) / f)
    }
    else {
        first <- "signal"
        pause <- durations[seq(2, npos - 1, by = 2)]
        signal <- durations[seq(1, npos - 1, by = 2)]
        start.signal <- positions[seq(1, npos - 1, by = 2)]
        end.signal <- positions[seq(2, npos - 1, by = 2)]
        if (start.signal > end.signal) start.signal <- c(0, start.signal)
    }

Let me know if anyone already encountered this problem.

Greetings,
Thibaut Marin-Cudraz
PhD Student
CNPS/ENES

messages.subject: Missing 1 second from every "readWave" loaded file when "units" specified?
messages.subject_clean: Missing 1 second from every "readWave" loaded file when "units" specified?
messages.body_plain:
I expect this is a tuneR problem rather than a seewave problem, but...

Whenever I load a .wav file using readWave and with "units" specified, it comes in with one single second missing from the file.  Is this a normal feature of the package?
....

wavefiles <- "H:/ARU Data/ARU Database FY15/TestforAutocorr/sel.01.ch01.180411.092334.43.r.SMHM1.0.3683.Table 1.wav"

z2<-readWave(wavefiles, units = "seconds" )
z2

 > z2<-readWave(wavefiles, units = "seconds" )
> z2

Wave Object
	Number of Samples:      104696
	Duration (seconds):     2.37
	Samplingrate (Hertz):   44100
	Channels (Mono/Stereo): Mono
	PCM (integer format):   TRUE
	Bit (8/16/24/32/64):    16

> z3<-readWave(pswavefiles)
> z3

Wave Object
	Number of Samples:      148796
	Duration (seconds):     3.37
	Samplingrate (Hertz):   44100
	Channels (Mono/Stereo): Mono
	PCM (integer format):   TRUE
	Bit (8/16/24/32/64):    16

>

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Missing 1 second from every "readWave" loaded file when "units" specified?
messages.subject_clean: [seewave] Missing 1 second from every "readWave" loaded file when "units" specified?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

This is because the argument 'from' has a default value of 1 (from=1) which is ok when you use the default value of units="samples", but when you use units="seconds" the function reads the .wav file starting after 1 s.

HTH

Jerome

messages.subject: Frequency limit for command spectro()
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have captured many bat sound @192kHz sampling frequency.
I will build an spectrogramm between 10 an 100 kHz to see all details of these sounds, but the upper frequency limit of the spectro() command is 48 kHz.

See png example plotted with the following command.
spectro(wave01,f=192000,flim=c(10,48))

When i made a plot with the command
spectro(wave01,f=96000,flim=c(10,48))
the spectrogramm is completly plotted but, of course, the frequency scale is wrong...

Do you have any tips for solving this case?

Bests regards

Daniel

messages.subject: Re: Frequency limit for command spectro()
messages.body_plain:
Hi Daniel,

You are building the spectrogram limiting the frequency axis by using flim, do that the output will show the frequencies in between 10-48kHz (flim=c(10,48)) in either commands.

Either way, if you have recorded with a 192kHz resolution, you will be able to build spectrograms up to 96kHz (half the sampling rate).

Hence, you should use:

spectro(wave01,f=192000,flim=c(10,96))

Best,

Carlos.
